description.value: Bell 2 Lodge sits directly on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway (Hwy 37) at km 248, offering fuel, cafe meals, and camping against a backdrop of the Skeena Mountains and Bell Irving River — a rare full-service stop on a long, remote stretch with no cell service for hundreds of kilometres.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website confirms Bell 2 Lodge is an active full-service wilderness resort on Highway 37 at km 248 in Northern BC, offering both lodge rooms and camping ('Stay in our log chalets or camp with us'). The cafe explicitly lists propane as a fuel type available on-site, and the site includes an availability-request system confirming reservations are accepted. OSM tags (power_supply=yes, sanitary_dump_station=yes, capacity=10, internet_access=wlan) characterize a caravan/RV-style campsite; no specific cyclist-only amenity details (showers, hiker-biker sites, laundry) are mentioned on the website, so those remain null.
concerns: OSM name is 'Bell II' but the website consistently uses 'Bell 2 Lodge' — minor format discrepancy.
OSM has no phone number listed; website provides (250) 275-4770 (local) and 1-888-499-4354 (toll-free).

OSM lists internet_access=wlan, but website states 'no cell phone service or internet services before and after the lodge' — this likely means the surrounding highway has no connectivity, not the lodge itself; OSM wifi tag may be valid for in-lodge use but warrants clarification.
OSM capacity=10 appears to refer to RV/caravan pitches; no hiker-biker specific campsite information is available on the website.
OSM has no street address; website describes only a highway kilometre-mark location (km 248, Hwy 37).
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Bell 2 Lodge is a well-established and actively operating stop on the remote Stewart-Cassiar Highway, offering camping, food, propane, and accommodation in a stretch of road with no other services for dozens of kilometres — a genuinely valuable listing for cycle tourists on this corridor.
enrichment_extras.notes: A critical resupply point for cyclists on the Stewart-Cassiar Highway. The lodge explicitly advises planning lodging 24–48 hours in advance due to no cell coverage on the surrounding road — relevant for touring cyclists approaching from either direction.

wow_evidence: rare full-service stop on a long, remote stretch with no cell service for hundreds of kilometres
